name: Hetzel Hall
use: Traditional-style residence hall, 141 students; first-year and upper-division
architect: Eric T. Huddleston (original, per AIA NH submission); Lavallee Brensinger Architects (2023-25 renovation) with contractor Wright-Ryan

renovations.what: First major renovation in its 100 years: full interior overhaul, new elevator (building underpinned with steel beams), air conditioning, more singles and private bathrooms, community kitchen and lounges, new roof and windows, two accessible entrances; reopened January 2025, grand opening June 7, 2025

facts.text: Built in 1925 and dedicated in June 1927 to Ralph Dorn Hetzel, New Hampshire College president 1917-1927, under whom the legislature made the college a university.
Designed by campus architect Eric Huddleston; a four-story Colonial Revival hall and the second building on what was then the east quadrangle.
Closed during the COVID-19 pandemic and reopened in January 2025 after its first significant renovation in 100 years.

The renovation added an elevator, air conditioning, more single rooms and private bathrooms, and a kitchen beside the first-floor lounge; the exterior got a new roof and windows while keeping its historic look.
The renovation was budgeted at $26 million for about 140 beds.
Housing says Hetzel filled faster than any other building in first-year room selection after reopening.
Address 63 Main Street, at a corner of campus beside downtown Durham; hall size 141 students; two private accessible suites and two full accessible bathrooms per floor.
AIA New Hampshire jurors praised the wood cabinetry, textiles, colours, furnishings and interior lighting, and noted blower-door results 20% better than before.

verdict: Huddleston's 1925 Colonial Revival hall on Main Street, gutted and reopened in 2025 with A/C, an elevator and private baths; it now fills first.
notes: Licensed photo (2013) predates the renovation; exterior is largely unchanged (brick, white trim, mansard-style dormer roof, balustraded terrace) but roof and windows were replaced. Reference lounge photo (UNH Housing, 2025) shows a bright room with three large wood-trimmed windows, wood-slat ceiling, new carpet and furniture: strong natural light, ordinary ceiling height. Old row's claim that the renovation won an award: the AIA NH page is a 2025 awards submission with juror comments; I could not confirm which award level, if any. Architect of the original is from the AIA submission, not the archives page. Cost ($26M) is the 2023 budget figure, not a final cost. Society19 page metadata says Dec 2024 but the text predates the renovation.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a handsome brick front with mansard dormers and a balustraded terrace; reference lounges are bright and new. Down from the old run's #2: exterior is good, not landmark, and condition 9 rather than 10.
